steps.what: Verify patient and examination identity and capture the radiologist's actual findings and limitations
Write the comprehensive interpretive report of findings, impression and relevant comparisons

loop.purpose: Turn radiologist-authored findings into a structured report draft
loop.input: Verified patient and examination metadata plus radiologist-captured findings, comparisons and limitations
loop.output: Draft report with traceable findings and impression
loop.check: Radiologist checks laterality, anatomy, measurements, comparison dates, negation, uncertainty, omitted findings and agreement between findings and impression
loop.stop: Missing finding support or two failed revisions returns the report to manual writing
loop.why_not_simpler: Use native report headings and fixed text first; variable interpretive prose needs a bounded loop

steps.what: Edit and check the finished interpretive report against the radiologist's findings and images

tasks.design: Use native structured headings in the {OTHER} radiology reporting system before a bounded loop formats the radiologist's captured findings into prose. The radiologist checks the complete report against the images; ordinary draft saves stay ungated, and communication to recipients is owned by the separate communication task.
tasks.previous_blocker: Radiologist-authored findings still require repetitive narrative formulation.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded prose draft can use captured findings without interpreting images independently.
tasks.still_hard: Subtle negation, laterality and uncertainty errors can change the clinical meaning.
tasks.human_edge: The radiologist owns the interpretation and the report's clinical meaning.
tasks.altitude: Assist report prose while retaining interpretation and final editing.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: bounded drafting can format clinician-authored findings but requires radiology-specific semantic checking.

assumptions: Shares and prose reduction are hypotheses, not measured radiology baselines.
OTHER means radiology image and reporting systems.
Actual image interpretation is produced by the radiologist in the imaging task; s1 counts capturing findings, measurements, laterality and uncertainty for this report.
No free ambient transcript or automated image diagnosis is assumed.
Final distribution and recipient communication are counted under 17252, avoiding duplicate report delivery.
unknowns: Current structured reporting and dictation use
research_questions: Does drafting still reduce prose work after checking every clinical qualifier and negative finding?

already_counted.description: Capture source findings in s1, check draft meaning in s2 and manually repair rejected prose in s3.

incremental.description: Amortised report-template and meaning-error regression review.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100. Initial prose removes 55*0.15=8.25 hours less 1 upkeep, net 7.25. Cautious case: unusual multifocal findings require almost complete manual rewriting, leaving only 1.3 hours of routine report phrasing removed and 0.3 net; repairs consume the rest of the nominal drafting benefit.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Perform or interpret diagnostic imaging procedures

steps.what: Review the clinical question, patient identity and relevant imaging history
Retrieve the actual diagnostic images and matching prior examinations for comparison
outputs: checked current and prior image display

steps.what: Interpret MRI, CT, PET, mammography, ultrasound or other diagnostic imaging outcomes
inputs: checked current and prior image display

steps.what: Enter actual image annotations and measurements that support the interpretation

tasks.design: Configure the native {OTHER} image viewer's prior-comparison display to reduce repeated study navigation. OTHER denotes radiology image archive and viewing software; the radiologist verifies study identity, reads the images and writes actual annotations, with comprehensive report prose counted separately.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding and arranging relevant prior studies can require repeated viewer navigation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native comparison layouts can bring matching existing studies into view without interpreting them.
tasks.still_hard: Image quality, clinical context and subtle pathology require radiologist judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The radiologist decides what the images mean for this patient.
tasks.altitude: Reduce image-navigation mechanics while retaining diagnostic interpretation.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: radiology viewers support native current-versus-prior study display layouts.

assumptions: This graph covers the interpretation branch of the stated perform-or-interpret task; a radiologist-performed procedure requires its actual physical steps and cannot inherit these shares.
Shares are unmeasured hypotheses; existing automatic prior display earns no new saving.
Current images are produced by the actual imaging acquisition workflow and prior studies already exist; s1 and s2 count identity, date and modality checks.
Missing or mismatched priors require manual retrieval and repair in s2, reducing the navigation benefit.
Annotations remain in s4; comprehensive report writing belongs to 17242 and procedure documentation to 17248.
research_questions: How much retrieval time is avoidable navigation after verifying the right patient and study?

already_counted.description: Check and repair study selection and manually retrieve missing priors in s2.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100. Native comparison display removes 15*0.20=3 navigation hours less 0.5 upkeep, net 2.5. Cautious case: most relevant priors are external and must be retrieved and aligned manually, leaving only 0.7 hours of local-study navigation removed and 0.2 net; reading and annotation remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Verify the actual procedure performed, technical details, complications and immediate patient outcome
Write the actual procedure performance, interpretation references and outcomes in the clinical record
outputs: draft procedure performance and outcome record

steps.what: Check the finished procedure record for completeness, accuracy and patient-specific exceptions
inputs: draft procedure performance and outcome record
outputs: checked procedure performance and outcome record

tasks.design: Configure the existing {OTHER} clinical procedure form to reuse verified examination identity and recurring field headings. OTHER means radiology clinical-record software; actual procedure details and exceptions remain authored and checked, and the ordinary author save has no approval gate or saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Identity fields and recurring procedure headings can be repeatedly entered with actual outcomes.
tasks.enabler_now: Native clinical forms can reuse stable metadata without inventing performance or outcome facts.
tasks.still_hard: Complications and departures from the expected procedure must be described accurately.
tasks.human_edge: The radiologist distinguishes what was planned from what actually happened.
tasks.altitude: Reduce a small amount of repeated form entry.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native clinical forms can reuse verified examination identity fields and procedure headings.

assumptions: Shares are unmeasured hypotheses for the procedure-record branch.
This is the actual clinical procedure record, read for subsequent care; comprehensive interpretive prose is owned by 17242 and is linked rather than rewritten.
The radiologist verifies actual event facts in s1; no automatic event extraction or normal-result assertion is assumed.
Already populated identity fields yield no additional saving.
unknowns: Separate record versus linked report practice
research_questions: How much actual record entry is repeated identity and headings rather than patient-specific documentation?

already_counted.description: Author actual procedure facts in s2 and check and repair the record in s3.

incremental.description: Amortised clinical form and identity-mapping checks.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100. Reused identity and headings remove 50*0.06=3 hours less 0.5 upkeep, net 2.5. Cautious case: an unusual intervention requires bespoke technical and complication documentation and only 0.7 hours of examination identity reuse remains, leaving 0.2 net; actual event writing and checking stay retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Communicate imaging findings to clinicians, patients and families

steps.what: Review the checked examination findings, urgency and authorised recipient or patient contact
Prepare the actual examination-result message with the correct report link and contact details
Check and approve the completed result message and exact authorised recipient
Send the approved examination-result message through the authorised clinical channel
Communicate examination results personally and answer the physician's, patient's or family's questions
outputs: explained diagnostic information and clarified questions

steps.what: Enter the actual result communication, recipient and agreed follow-up in the clinical record
inputs: explained diagnostic information and clarified questions

tasks.design: Reuse the native {OTHER} clinical-result message layout and checked report reference while retaining clinical explanation and recipient checks. OTHER is the clinical communication and patient-record system; approve the finished message before its separate send, then write the actual communication event without a gate on that ordinary save.
tasks.previous_blocker: Result messages can repeat report-identification and contact structure.
tasks.enabler_now: A native message layout reuses this structure without summarising diagnostic meaning.
tasks.still_hard: Urgency, uncertainty, distress and questions need personal clinical communication.
tasks.human_edge: The radiologist makes the result understandable and resolves clinical questions.
tasks.altitude: Small preparation reuse while retaining personal communication.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: clinical messaging layouts can reuse checked report references and contact structure.

assumptions: Shares are unmeasured hypotheses for a written-message plus discussion branch; oral-only and automatically routed reports require different shares.
The checked report is produced under 17242, so its prose is not counted again here.
Recipient identity and authority are verified in s1; no unrestricted family disclosure is assumed.
Urgent direct communication is not delayed for the written-message path.
The actual communication entry already supports follow-up care; no new unused log is introduced.
unknowns: Mix of verbal and written communication
research_questions: Is any actual message preparation still repeated after existing routing is excluded?

already_counted.description: Prepare actual message content in s2, check the final recipient-bound version in s3 and record the actual event in s6.

approvals.approved_version: s3 exact result-message version, report reference and named authorised recipient; any edit voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100. Reused message structure removes 10*0.10=1 hour less 0.3 upkeep, net 0.7. Cautious case: a complex cross-provider result needs bespoke wording and manual destination confirmation, leaving only 0.4 hours of report-identification reuse and 0.1 net; send, explanation and actual communication record stay retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce selected reporting and navigation mechanics while retaining image interpretation and clinical communication.
skills_to_grow: Check clinical negation and uncertainty in drafts
Separate report authorship from recipient-bound communication
role.ambitious_version: A radiologist uses reliable reporting and viewing tools while personally owning diagnostic meaning and patient communication.
